storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: Wave 7 still permits broker record loss, and startup failures can leave a live broker without a usable PID record.

Findings:
- [high] BLOCKING: stale cleanup can delete a replacement broker’s record (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:295-298)
  The re-read is locked, but the endpoint comparison and unlink are not. After this comparison, another stale caller can clear the old record and claim a new broker; this caller then unlinks the new record. The compare/unlink race existed in v1.4.0 and remains open despite Wave 7.
  Recommendation: Make conditional record deletion atomic under the state lock at every caller, and test replacement between comparison and deletion.
- [high] BLOCKING: a failed PID save strands a spawned broker (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:332-335)
  The broker is spawned before the provisional record is updated with its PID. If this save throws, no failed-start teardown runs; the child may keep running behind a pid-null record. A later start can either reuse that incomplete record or clear it as `no-pid` and spawn a second broker.
  Recommendation: Handle post-spawn save failures by retaining the child handle, performing verified teardown, and clearing the claim only after exit is confirmed.
- [high] BLOCKING: SessionEnd can terminate a broker still starting (plugins/codex/scripts/session-lifecycle-hook.mjs:354-369)
  Startup saves the PID and identity before the endpoint is ready. If another session ends then, a connection error is treated as an idle broker; this guard calls it `starting` only while PID is null. SessionEnd can therefore kill the new broker during its readiness wait and disrupt the new request.
  Recommendation: Persist a startup state independent of PID presence and keep provisional brokers out of SessionEnd teardown until startup completes.

Next steps:
- Fix the three startup and cleanup paths, then exercise their interleavings in targeted tests and Windows E2E.
